verdicts.summary: Validates (0 errors). Every confidence-3 event I opened (12) says what its note claims. Five events were wrong or undated at confidence 1 and I corrected them on pages I opened: Italian Somaliland's British administration ends 1 April 1950, not 1960; the Libya occupation starts February 1943, not 1944, and leaves out the French Fezzan (2,015 cells); Eritrea ends 15 September 1952; Ethiopia ends 31 January 1942. What remains is thin by design under the 14-page budget: the south-eastern Libya block (1,837 cells, 1905-1929, then 280 cells to 1935) has no event; five confidence-1 events (found, Botswana 1890, Matabeleland 1894, Swaziland 1908, dissolve); and the Ogaden and Haud (British until 1948/1955 according to the ethiopia dossier) are released in 1942. Cross-dossier mismatches are mostly counterpart-slug disagreements, because other dossiers write british-colonial-empire or british-south-africa-company where this one writes british-africa.

fixes.what: Italian Somaliland occupation_end dated 1960 at confidence 1; the British administration ended on 1 April 1950, so 637k km2 was hatched British for ten years too long.
fixes.why: Trust Territory of Somaliland: 'The British continued to administer the area until 1 April 1950' (infobox 'Established: 1 April 1950'); British Somaliland page: in 1960 it 'united with the Trust Territory of Somalia'.
fixes.fix: year 1950, month 4, confidence 3, source Trust_Territory_of_Somaliland (added to sources[]), ledger re-sorted.

fixes.what: Libya occupation_start dated 1944 at confidence 1 and drawn over the whole of Libya, Fezzan included, which was French-administered.
fixes.why: British Military Administration (Libya): 'By February 1943, the last German and Italian soldiers were driven from Libya and the Allied occupation of Libya began' (infobox 13 May 1943); 'while the French controlled Fezzan'. Libya minus Fezzan resolves to 3,424 cells, matching Cliopatria's 3,427.
fixes.fix: year 1943, month 2, confidence 2 (text and infobox disagree), region {minus: [Libya, region Fezzan]}, source British_Military_Administration_(Libya) (added).

fixes.what: The Nile valley is lost by mahdist-state at Dongola (1896-09), Abu Hamed (1897-08) and Omdurman (1898-09), all with counterpart british-africa, but this dossier gains nothing until the condominium (1899-06). Between contest_end 1898 and June 1899, the conquered valley belongs to neither side.
fixes.why: mahdist-state /ledger/14-16; Anglo-Egyptian Sudan: 'Kitchener led military campaigns from 1896 to 1898' (no dates for Dongola or Abu Hamed on that page).
fixes.fix: Add gains of Dongola (1896-09), Abu Hamed (1897-08) and Omdurman/Khartoum (1898-09) from mahdist-state using that dossier's pages, or move the River Nile, Northern and Khartoum gain to 1898-09 at contest_end.

fixes.fix: One sentence in notes naming the rows that hold them (british-gold-coast, federal-republic-of-nigeria, sultanate-of-zanzibar, and so on).

thin.what is missing: The 1,837-cell south-eastern Libya block (16.4-25.0 E, 19.7-29.8 N, Kufra and the Libyan Desert), British from 1905 to 1929 with no event; probably the British sphere east of the 1899 Anglo-French line or Egypt's undefined western frontier, ended by the 1925 Italo-Egyptian frontier (Jaghbub) and the Italian occupation of Kufra (1931).
The 280 Libya cells of 1932-1935 (19.5-25.0 E, 19.7-21.9 N) are likely the Sarra Triangle, ceded by Britain to Italy in 1934; no event.

Swaziland 1908 gain at confidence 1 (source Second Boer War, which is silent); the swaziland dossier has vassal_start 1903 (counterpart british-colonial-empire). Date the British protectorate or High Commission territory (1903/1906) and settle gain against vassal_start with that dossier.
Botswana 1890 gain (the northern Bechuanaland Protectorate) at confidence 1.
Matabeleland 1894 at confidence 1, the year taken from the ndebele-kingdom dossier (loss 1894-01 after the First Matabele War, 1893-10 to 1894-01). It needs a month and the contest pair.
Found and dissolve are Cliopatria bridges at confidence 1 (inherent in a composite row; acceptable).

The 1916 occupation gives all of Tanzania except Kigoma to Britain, although Belgian troops held Tabora (19 September 1916) and by 1917 'occupied one-third of German East Africa' (Belgian Congo page). The Anglo-Belgian occupation line of 1916-1917 is not drawn.
Republic of Liberia records the Parrot's Beak as a 1903-06 gain from british-africa and a 1911-01 loss to it (the January 1911 exchange also moved land the other way); this dossier has neither.

verdicts.summary: Validates (0 errors, 0 warnings). Years are in order and inside the life (1908-11 to 1962-07); found and dissolve sit at start and end; contest and occupation pairs close. The 1890-1898 shapes are marked wrong in favour of congo-free-state, which has its own keyframes (congo-free-state_1885, _1895) and the mirror dissolve (1908-11). Every event I opened (8 of 14) is confirmed with its year and month. The area matches (ratio 1.01). Ruanda-Urundi is treated as part of the colony from 1922 although the Belgian Congo page says 'These areas did not become part of the Belgian Congo'; the notes argue this from the 1 March 1926 administrative merger and ask for a separate ruanda-urundi dossier, which I accept as a declared judgement. The Kigoma cross-check mismatch is assigned to british-africa. I could not break it.

The 1911-1915 shape carries 163 Republic-of-the-Congo cells (the author counts 133); they are removed on an area comparison alone. A page on the Congo-French Equatorial Africa frontier would confirm it.
